chancellor-baptist-church.assessment: Chancellor Baptist's doctrinal statement is genuinely solid — they affirm Scripture as God's Word, salvation through Christ alone, eternal security, baptism by immersion, Great Commission evangelism. The church's mission statement (pointing people to Christ and into His church) is clear and healthy. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: unlike SBC, BGAV is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream that parted ways over inerrancy and women's ordination. That doesn't automatically mean Chancellor is progressive — many BGAV churches are theologically conservative at the local level — but the accountability structure is to a moderate denomination. Before joining, Moop should ask: Does Chancellor have an elder board? What is the stance on women in pastoral roles? Pastor Cameron West's background and convictions are unknown — worth a direct conversation.

christ-church-morrisville-nc.assessment: Christ Church is a CREC (Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches) congregation meeting in Morrisville, North Carolina, led by Pastor Duane Garner — an ACBC-certified biblical counselor who also serves as Presiding Minister of the CREC’s Augustine Presbytery. It is confessional and covenantal: the Bible is “absolutely authoritative,” the historic Reformed confessions and catechisms are its doctrinal summary, worship follows the covenant-renewal pattern with Psalm-singing, and the congregation is governed by a plurality of male elders and deacons. Its culture is family-integrated, classically educated, and robustly counter-secular. An acquaintance of MOOP recommended it as “super solid” — free of the wokeness, CRT, and female-leadership concerns this directory screens for. It earns green across all ten categories.

christ-church-waco-tx-acna.assessment: Christ Church Waco is an ACNA parish in the Diocese of Fort Worth, led by Priest-in-Charge Fr. Jeff Logan, who arrived in October 2025 after 22 years as a Navy chaplain. His academic credentials are unusually strong: B.A. from DePauw, M.Div. from the Episcopal Theological Seminary of the Southwest, and D.Min. from Fuller Theological Seminary. The parish maintains a full liturgical rhythm: Sunday 8:00 AM and 10:45 AM Holy Eucharist with 9:30 AM Catechesis, plus a Wednesday Noon Eucharist. Supported by Fr. Andrew Hollinger (Diocesan Curate, M.Div. Nashotah House 2024) and Rev. Thomas Hunter (Deacon, ordained 2024). Self-describes as 'a church of the great commandment, the great commission, and the Great Tradition.' ACNA 39 Articles framework aligns with MOOP's rubric. Strong green-rated Anglican option for Central Texas.

christ-kirk-dc.assessment: Christ Kirk DC is a confessional Reformed, evangelical church in Washington, DC affiliated with the Christ Church Moscow tradition (Doug Wilson, author and theologian). The church affirms the Apostles' Creed, Nicene Creed, Chalcedonian Definition, and Westminster Confession of Faith — a strong confessional foundation. Preaching from Pastor Garrett Craw is expository, Word-centered, and theologically serious. Strengths: genuine commitment to Reformation doctrine, strong complementarianism, serious men's discipleship, winsome confessional faith in an antagonistic cultural context. Caution: the Doug Wilson association brings controversy — Wilson's provocative cultural commentary and church planting theology attract both admirers and fierce critics; men should evaluate this association thoughtfully. The church has been targeted by progressive activist groups, which speaks to both its clear doctrinal stance and its cultural visibility. For a man wanting serious Reformed theology and strong masculine leadership culture in DC, Christ Kirk is worth serious consideration.

Overall a green-eligible, solidly orthodox Wesleyan church worth further on-the-ground review.

christ-the-redeemer-anglican-fairfax.assessment: Christ the Redeemer Anglican is an ACNA congregation in Fairfax, VA under Rector Dean Schultz in the Diocese of the Mid-Atlantic. ACNA was formed as a breakaway from the Episcopal Church to preserve biblical Anglicanism — it holds to the authority of Scripture, the orthodox creeds, the Nicene faith, and biblical complementarianism (male eldership). The church follows the Sunday liturgy in the Book of Common Prayer including psalm-singing, Scripture readings, preaching, the Lord's Table, and intercessory prayer. Currently meeting primarily online via Zoom, which limits in-person community building. For men who value liturgical Anglican worship rooted in Scripture with ACNA accountability, this is a sound option — though the online-primary format warrants verification of current in-person fellowship opportunities.

church-at-clarendon-arlington.assessment: The Church at Clarendon has a female senior pastor — Pastor Danielle Bridgeforth — which places it outside the bounds of biblical complementarianism (1 Tim 2:12; 3:1-7). The American Baptist Churches USA (ABC) denomination is theologically moderate-to-liberal and affirms women's ordination, contrasting sharply with the SBC's Baptist Faith & Message 2000. The church may have sincere believers and Christ-centered sermons, but the pastoral leadership structure contradicts clear New Testament instruction on male-only elder/pastor roles. For a man serious about building his spiritual life in a doctrinally sound environment, The Church at Clarendon is not recommended as a primary home church.

church-of-incarnation-richmond.assessment: Church of the Incarnation is an ACNA church plant serving western Henrico County, meeting at Gayton Road Christian Church on Sundays at 9am. The Anglican Church in North America (ACNA) formed in 2009 when conservative Anglicans broke from the progressive Episcopal Church (TEC) over Scripture authority, sexuality, and leadership. ACNA holds to the 39 Articles, male clergy, traditional Anglican liturgy, and biblical sexual ethics — a clean break from TEC's progressive drift. The church's stated core values are compelling: 'Biblical teaching for the head and the heart; Spiritual formation through liturgy and sacrament; A life of prayer together; Gospel care for those in need; Discipleship of the next generation.' This is Word-and-sacrament Anglicanism done right. Strong option for men who love liturgical worship rooted in Scripture.

church-of-the-advent-dc.assessment: Church of the Advent is one of Washington DC's most interesting evangelical Anglican church plants. Founded in 2007 by Tommy Hinson from a prayer meeting in Columbia Heights, Advent belongs to the ACNA — the orthodox Anglican body that separated from the theologically liberal Episcopal Church (TEC). The church explicitly describes its mission as 'seeking the flourishing of Washington, DC,' combining robust liturgical worship with urban community engagement. The ACNA framework provides the theological guardrails: Jerusalem Declaration, 39 Articles, male-only ordination, and confessional accountability. For any man in DC seeking Anglican worship without the progressive drift of TEC, Church of the Advent is a premier choice.

churchome-seattle-wa.assessment: Churchome — formerly The City Church, founded by Wendell Smith in 1992 — is now led by Wendell's son Judah Smith and Judah's wife Chelsea Smith as co-lead pastors. Chelsea holds the same top pastoral title as Judah and preaches Sunday services. Church Clarity scores Churchome "Clear: Egalitarian" on women in leadership. Per MOOP rubric (female pastor at senior level → RED), this is a hard RED on gender and leadership. Additional concerns: (1) LGBTQ policy is publicly Undisclosed — Chelsea Smith answered the gay-pastor question with rhetorical inclusion rather than a policy answer; (2) T.D. Jakes — historically associated with Oneness/modalist Christology — joined the Churchome board around 2021, raising Trinity-adjacency concerns even though Churchome itself is formally Trinitarian; (3) the celebrity-pastor culture (Justin Bieber and other A-list members) and Churchome app-driven model represent a particular branch of attractional evangelicalism that prioritizes accessibility over doctrinal precision. The Belltown Seattle campus at 2700 1st Ave is the flagship location. Judah Smith is a gifted communicator; the preaching is grace-focused, narrative, and culturally engaged. But the egalitarian leadership structure, LGBTQ ambiguity, and board composition make this RED per MOOP convictions. This is NOT Mars Hill (which dissolved 2014 under Mark Driscoll); Churchome is a different church with a different doctrinal posture. Adam visited Churchome in Seattle.

Chelsea Smith's public response to gay pastor question was rhetorically inclusive without policy clarity ("we love everybody"). 2022 abortion comments from Chelsea Smith publicly criticized as evasive. Cultural-alignment concerns track LGBTQ ambiguity + celebrity-pastor culture (Justin Bieber etc.).
score_notes.preaching: Judah Smith preaches accessible, narrative, topical messages with cultural-relevance emphasis. Not expository verse-by-verse. Yellow.
score_notes.mission: Multi-site expansion + Churchome app + global media reach; classic megachurch attractional model. Specific Great Commission framing not foregrounded in About.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's ministry surfaced on About or homepage. Megachurch model does not prioritize sex-specific discipleship.
score_notes.denominational: Non-denominational independent; no external accountability structure beyond internal board. T.D. Jakes on board raises Trinity-adjacency concern. RED per MOOP rubric.
